title: Japan Needs Higher Interest Rates
gist: Koichi Hamada argues the cheap yen is hurting Japan's economy: OECD PPP puts fair value near 93 yen/USD versus an actual 150-160. The piece (truncated excerpt) sets up the case for higher Bank of Japan interest rates.

insights.claim: The OECD reports a purchasing-power-parity equilibrium exchange rate of about 93 yen per dollar between Japan and the US, versus an actual rate hovering at 150-160.
insights.speaker: Koichi Hamada
insights.so_what: A 40%+ gap between PPP and spot frames the yen as deeply undervalued, supporting yen-appreciation or BoJ-tightening theses.

insights.claim: The weak yen (yen yasu) has made Japan very cheap for foreign tourists, for example about $20 per person for a high-quality restaurant lunch in Sapporo, but is hard on the Japanese economy.
insights.speaker: Koichi Hamada
insights.so_what: Inbound tourism strength is a symptom of currency weakness, not just a growth tailwind; watch import-cost and real-wage pressure.

insights.claim: The author's framing, via the title and PPP argument, is that Japan needs higher interest rates to counter the cheap yen.
insights.speaker: Koichi Hamada
insights.so_what: Supports positioning for further BoJ hikes and yen strength, though the excerpt gives no detailed policy path.
